points.t: Older person with itchy ‘eczema’ or hives that won’t settle, then **tense** blisters on limbs and trunk.
Autoantibodies to BP180/BP230 split the skin **below** the epidermis. Gliptins and loop diuretics trigger it.
Refer for biopsy; review gliptins; doxycycline 200 mg daily ± superpotent topical steroid.
Ocular mucous membrane pemphigoid (blindness), pemphigoid gestationis, steroid toxicity in the frail.

cause.lead: Autoantibodies unglue the epidermis from the dermis.
points: IgG (± IgE) against **BP180** and **BP230** in the hemidesmosome.
Complement, eosinophils and proteases → a **subepidermal** split.
A full-thickness roof keeps the blister **tense**.
**Drug triggers**: **gliptins** (especially vildagliptin), loop diuretics, spironolactone, PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

visuals.caption: Level of the split. Left, bullous pemphigoid: below the whole epidermis, so the roof is thick and the blister stays tense. Right, pemphigus: inside the epidermis, so the roof is thin and the blister is flaccid and breaks.
visuals.alt: Two skin cross-sections comparing a tense subepidermal blister with a flaccid intraepidermal blister

features.lead: Two phases: itch first, blisters later.
points: **Prodrome**: weeks to months of itch, urticarial or eczematous plaques. Often mislabelled ‘eczema’ or ‘scabies’.
**Bullous phase**: **tense**, clear or haemorrhagic bullae on an urticarial base or normal skin.
**Sites**: flexural limbs, inner thighs, groin, lower abdomen, trunk.
Mucosa in only ~10–20% (mild). Nikolsky usually **negative**. Heals without scars.

visuals.caption: Typical distribution: inner arms and forearms, inner thighs, groin, lower abdomen and trunk.
visuals.alt: Older adult outline with blisters on flexural limbs, groin and trunk

items.name: Non-bullous phase
items.t: Itchy urticated plaques for weeks to months.

items.name: Tense bullae
items.t: Clear and haemorrhagic blisters on an urticated base.

items.name: Pemphigoid gestationis
items.t: Starts **around the umbilicus**, 2nd–3rd trimester or postpartum.

points: Age, neurological disease (dementia, Parkinson’s, stroke, MS).
**Drug list**: gliptins, loop diuretics, spironolactone, checkpoint inhibitors.
Tense vs flaccid blisters; Nikolsky.
Mouth, eyes, genitals; extent and infection.
Biopsy: **subepidermal** blister with eosinophils.
Perilesional **DIF**: linear IgG / C3 at the BMZ.
Serology: anti-BP180 / BP230 ELISA.
Glucose / HbA1c, BP, bone health.
Renal function, baseline weight.

cards.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
cards.clue: Flaccid blisters that rupture at once; mucosa prominent; Nikolsky positive.

cards.name: Scabies
cards.clue: Pre-bullous mimic in care homes: burrows, other residents itching.

cards.name: Urticaria
cards.clue: Wheals fade within 24 h; no blisters.

cards.name: Bullous impetigo
cards.clue: Flaccid blister, collarette erosions; often children.

cards.name: Linear IgA disease
cards.clue: ‘String of beads’ annular blisters; can be drug-induced.

differentials.more: Also: drug eruption, prurigo, MMP, EBA (scarring, milia), bullous insect bites, bullous cellulitis, oedema blisters, bullous tinea.

manage.lead: Dermatology confirms and leads. The IP prescribes and monitors under specialist advice.

points: **Stop or switch a gliptin** with the patient and team; review loop diuretics.
Puncture tense blisters, leave the roof on; non-adherent dressings; emollients.

rx.dur: With superpotent TCS for the first weeks
rx.note: BLISTER: non-inferior for short-term control and significantly safer than prednisolone.

rx.dose: ~20–40 g/day split over the body (spare face)
rx.note: Safer than prednisolone 1 mg/kg (French RCT). 500 g packs, nurse application.
Steroid card, bone protection, glucose and BP monitoring.

points: Azathioprine, MMF, methotrexate, dapsone.
Dupilumab or omalizumab (check UK commissioning); rituximab or IVIG.

limits.t: Full glass of water, upright, not at bedtime. 2–3 h from calcium, iron, antacids, zinc. Photosensitivity; INR may rise.
Quantify (~30 g/day), count FTUs, warn about thinning and purpura.

items.t: Extensive blistering or secondary infection in a frail patient.
Eye redness, grittiness or scarring with oral erosions (**MMP**): same-week ophthalmology, same day if vision affected.
Blistering in **pregnancy** starting round the umbilicus: dermatology + obstetrics.

pearls.t: ‘Itchy elderly patient with eczema that won’t settle’ may be **BP before the blisters**.
In care homes, **exclude scabies** in parallel: they can coexist.
Gliptin BP is often **non-inflammatory** with little redness. Check the repeat list.

quiz.a: The split is subepidermal, so the whole epidermis forms a thick roof.

quiz.q: Which drug class is the best-established trigger?

quiz.a: Linear IgG and/or C3 along the basement membrane zone.

quiz.q: Treatment for mild–moderate generalised BP in a frail 85-year-old?
quiz.a: Doxycycline 200 mg once daily plus superpotent topical steroid at first (BLISTER: safer than prednisolone).

quiz.q: Gritty red eyes with oral erosions suggest what?
quiz.a: Mucous membrane pemphigoid: same-week ophthalmology, same day if vision is affected.
